evidence.finding: Logged-in agents fell from 49 before the incident to 44 at 09:15 and ultimately 33; the post-incident mean declined 26.72%.
Productive agents fell from 46 at 09:00 to 41 at 09:15 and ultimately 31; the post-incident mean declined 25.58%.
Scheduled staffing remained constant at 49 while the scheduled-to-logged gap increased from zero to as many as 16 agents.
The only recorded event was a center-wide workforce notice at 09:15 reporting multiple same-day absences; no routing or platform event was recorded.
Mean service level fell from 90.34% before the incident to 66.86% afterward, a 23.48-point decline.
Mean ASA increased from 25.21 to 56.66 seconds after incident start, a 124.74% rise.
Mean offered calls increased only 5.97%, making demand a contributing pressure rather than the primary cause.

primary_root_cause_detail: Multiple same-day absences caused logged-in and productive staffing to fall beginning at 09:15 despite unchanged scheduled headcount. The resulting capacity deficit aligns with the sharp ASA increase and service-level decline.
recommended_actions: Activate same-day absence coverage and overflow procedures when logged-in staffing falls below plan.
Alert workforce management on scheduled-to-logged gaps at interval start and escalate persistent deficits.
Pre-position cross-skilled backup coverage for moderate demand increases during reduced staffing.
Review the cause and notification timing of the same-day absences and update contingency staffing plans.

rejected_hypotheses.reason: Offered volume rose only 5.97%, insufficient to explain the much larger service-level and ASA deterioration compared with the documented 26.72% logged-in staffing loss.
AHT decreased 0.32% after incident start rather than increasing.
No routing-change event was recorded, while the center-wide staffing loss directly coincided with degradation.
No platform event was recorded; the sole event was a same-day absence notice corroborated by staffing data.

stakeholder_summary: The service-level breach was most likely caused by same-day absences. Logged-in capacity began falling exactly at 09:15 while scheduled headcount remained unchanged, and productive staffing declined in parallel. Moderate volume growth added pressure, but AHT, routing, and platform explanations were not supported.
